_note: Metals, minerals and components that branch nodes consume and no other file here makes. Yields are stoichiometry or composition; heat is a thermodynamic floor; labour is borrowed from a named neighbouring entry or left out, and says so.

cobalt_ore_kg.basis: per tonne of hand-sorted cobalt arsenide and arsenate ore (smaltite, cobaltite, erythrite) from a vein deposit
cobalt_ore_kg.yield_basis: EXTRACTED. Grade belongs to the smelting recipe that consumes this ore. Cobalt minerals occur in hard-rock veins with nickel and silver arsenides, so the mining hours are copied from copper_ore_kg (hard-rock vein), not from a softer deposit. Hand-sorting the rich fraction from the vein rock is not costed separately, a heuristic gap.

vanadium_ore_kg.basis: per tonne of dressed vanadinite or carnotite concentrate from an oxidised lead or uranium-vanadium deposit
vanadium_ore_kg.yield_basis: EXTRACTED. Grade belongs to the recipe that consumes this concentrate. Vanadium minerals form in the oxidised zone of lead veins (vanadinite) and in sandstone-hosted deposits (carnotite), dressed by hand and gravity. Labour is copied from sphalerite_kg, another dressed vein-mineral concentrate.

beryl_kg.basis: per tonne of hand-cobbed beryl crystal from a granite pegmatite
beryl_kg.yield_basis: EXTRACTED. Beryl (Be3Al2Si6O18) occurs as large crystals in pegmatites and is picked out by hand, so this is hard-rock digging at the copper_ore_kg rate; sorting is not costed separately. The beryllium content is a property of the mineral and is stated in the recipe that consumes it.

rutile_kg.basis: per tonne of rutile (TiO2) concentrate separated from heavy-mineral beach or river sand
rutile_kg.yield_basis: EXTRACTED. Rutile is a heavy mineral in placer sands at the order of a few percent by mass of the sand (assumed 2%, so about 50 tonnes of sand per tonne of rutile). The digging and washing hours per tonne of sand are copied from sand_quartz_kg (6 hours per tonne of washed sand) and multiplied by that 50, giving 300. Magnetic and electrostatic separation of the heavy fraction is not costed, a heuristic gap.

magnesium_chloride_kg.basis: per tonne of magnesium chloride recovered from the bittern left after solar salt has crystallised from seawater
magnesium_chloride_kg.yield_basis: EXTRACTED from seawater. Seawater carries about 1.29 g of magnesium per kg, which is 5.1 g of MgCl2 per kg (95.21/24.305 times the magnesium figure), against about 27 g of NaCl per kg, so a tonne of MgCl2 needs about 5.3 times the seawater volume a tonne of salt does. Labour is salt_solar_kg's 15 labourer-hours per tonne multiplied by that ratio, about 79. Purification of the bittern and dehydration of the salt are not costed here, a heuristic gap.

cobalt_kg.basis: per tonne of metallic cobalt from roasted arsenide ore, carbon-reduced
cobalt_kg.yield_basis: STOICHIOMETRY AND ASSUMED GRADE. Dressed cobalt arsenide ore is taken as 20% cobalt (pure cobaltite is 35% and smaltite about 28%, diluted by gangue after sorting), recovered at 85% through roasting off the arsenic, then leaching and precipitation as oxide, so 1000/(0.20*0.85) = 5882 kg of ore. Reduction CoO + C -> Co + CO needs 12.011/58.933 = 0.204 kg carbon per kg cobalt. Heat is the thermodynamic floor: the reaction takes about 127 kJ per mole of cobalt (formation enthalpies of CoO and CO), 2155 MJ per tonne, plus heating and melting cobalt to 1495 C at about 0.45 kJ/kg/K and 260 kJ/kg latent heat, about 920 MJ, total about 3080 MJ. Arsenic fume is discarded uncosted. Labour is copied from tungsten_kg, a comparable roast, leach and reduce chain.

magnesium_kg.basis: per tonne of magnesium metal by electrolysis of molten magnesium chloride
magnesium_kg.yield_basis: FARADAY'S LAW AND STOICHIOMETRY. MgCl2 -> Mg + Cl2 needs 95.21/24.305 = 3.917 kg salt per kg metal, 5% lost as fume and spillage, so 4123 kg. Electrical energy is the decomposition voltage (about 2.5 V at 700 C) times two electrons per atom times the Faraday constant, 19.85 MJ per kg, divided by an assumed 85% current efficiency, giving about 23350 MJ per tonne; real cells draw more, so this is a floor. Heat to bring the salt to 700 C and melt it is sensible heat at about 0.8 kJ/kg/K plus 0.45 MJ/kg fusion, about 4050 MJ. Chlorine is a by-product not credited. Labour is copied from aluminium_kg, the other molten-salt electrolysis in this directory.

vanadium_kg.basis: per tonne of vanadium metal by aluminothermic reduction of vanadium pentoxide
vanadium_kg.yield_basis: STOICHIOMETRY AND ASSUMED GRADE. Vanadinite Pb5(VO4)3Cl is 10.8% vanadium; a dressed concentrate is taken as 9.7% (90% mineral), and leaching to V2O5 and reduction recover 70% overall, so 1000/(0.097*0.70) = 14728 kg concentrate. Reduction 3 V2O5 + 10 Al -> 6 V + 5 Al2O3 needs 10*26.98/(6*50.94) = 0.883 kg aluminium per kg vanadium, taken at 10% excess as chromium_kg does, 971 kg. The reaction is strongly exothermic and self-sustaining, so no external heat is listed. Labour is copied from chromium_kg, the same aluminothermic step.

titanium_kg.basis: per tonne of titanium sponge by the magnesium reduction of titanium tetrachloride (Kroll process)
titanium_kg.yield_basis: STOICHIOMETRY. TiO2 is 47.867/79.866 = 59.9% titanium, so 1.668 kg rutile per kg metal, at 90% recovery 1854 kg. Chlorination TiO2 + 2 Cl2 + 2 C -> TiCl4 + 2 CO needs 2*12.011/47.867 = 0.502 kg carbon per kg titanium, at 90% 558 kg. Reduction TiCl4 + 2 Mg -> Ti + 2 MgCl2 needs 2*24.305/47.867 = 1.016 kg magnesium per kg titanium, with 5% loss 1069 kg. The magnesium chloride by-product is not recycled and chlorine is not counted. Heat is the vacuum distillation of 3978 kg of MgCl2 at about 1000 C: 0.8 kJ/kg/K sensible plus 1.43 MJ/kg vaporisation, about 8870 MJ. Labour is copied from tungsten_kg, a comparable multi-stage extraction.

cadmium_kg.basis: per tonne of cadmium metal recovered from zinc-plant solution by zinc-dust cementation
cadmium_kg.yield_basis: STOICHIOMETRY. Cadmium is a trace constituent of zinc ore; the cadmium-bearing cake is a by-product of the zinc plant and its ore is already carried by zinc's own price, so only its separation is costed here. The cake is leached, CdO + H2SO4 -> CdSO4 + H2O, needing 98.08/112.41 = 0.873 kg acid per kg cadmium (873 kg, not regenerated here), then Cd2+ + Zn -> Cd + Zn2+ needs 65.38/112.41 = 0.582 kg zinc per kg cadmium, taken at 10% excess as chromium_kg's reductant is, 640 kg. Melting and casting the sponge is 0.23 kJ/kg/K to 321 C plus 55 kJ/kg fusion, about 130 MJ. The ore and leach reagents are carried by zinc's own price, a heuristic gap. Labour is copied from nickel_kg's refining hours.

xenon_g.basis: per 1000 grams of xenon separated from the krypton-xenon fraction of liquid oxygen
xenon_g.yield_basis: ATMOSPHERIC ABUNDANCE. Xenon is 0.087 ppm of air by volume against 20.95% oxygen, so 4.15e-7 mole of xenon per mole of oxygen; it is less volatile and concentrates in the liquid oxygen sump. One kilogram is 7.617 mol, carried by 1.835e7 mol = 587 kg = 411 m3 of oxygen at 1.429 kg/m3, and at an assumed 50% capture 822 m3 of oxygen_m3 passes through. That charges xenon the whole oxygen price although oxygen is also sold, a heuristic overcharge. Electrical energy is the ideal work of concentrating xenon from 4.15e-7 to unity at 90 K, R*T*ln(1/x) = 11.0 kJ/mol = 0.084 MJ per kg, a floor. Labour is inside the oxygen plant's own hours.

copper_beryllium_kg.basis: per tonne of copper-beryllium alloy, 1.9% beryllium by mass, by carbothermic reduction of beryllia in a copper bath
copper_beryllium_kg.yield_basis: COMPOSITION AND STOICHIOMETRY. Age-hardening copper-beryllium is about 1.9% beryllium. That is 19 kg beryllium per tonne; beryl is 5.03% beryllium (3*9.012/537.5) and taken as 70% recovered through opening and reduction, so 19/(0.0503*0.70) = 540 kg. BeO + C -> Be + CO needs 1.333 kg carbon per kg beryllium, 25.3 kg. Copper is 981 kg with the 2% melt loss bronze_kg uses, 1001 kg. Heat is a floor: the reduction takes about 499 kJ per mole beryllium (formation enthalpies of BeO and CO), 55.4 MJ/kg, 1052 MJ for 19 kg, plus heating and melting 981 kg copper (0.385 kJ/kg/K to 1085 C and 205 kJ/kg fusion), about 610 MJ; total 1665 MJ at about 2000 C, which only arc heating reaches. Reagents to open the beryl are not costed. Alloying labour is copied from bronze_kg.

cemented_carbide_kg.basis: per tonne of tungsten carbide with 6% cobalt binder, liquid-phase sintered
cemented_carbide_kg.yield_basis: COMPOSITION AND STOICHIOMETRY. The standard cutting grade is 94% tungsten carbide and 6% cobalt by mass. WC is 183.84/195.85 = 93.9% tungsten, so 0.94*0.939 = 882.4 kg tungsten and 57.6 kg carbon (12.011/195.85 per kg WC), plus 60 kg cobalt; the inputs sum to 1000. Heat is sintering to about 1450 C, taken as 0.3 kJ/kg/K sensible heat, about 450 MJ, with the cobalt going liquid. Labour is copied from tungsten_kg's furnace hours, the same powder-metallurgy consolidation, which includes chemical steps this one lacks and so overstates.

silicon_carbide_kg.basis: per tonne of silicon carbide from an Acheson resistance furnace
silicon_carbide_kg.yield_basis: STOICHIOMETRY. SiO2 + 3 C -> SiC + 2 CO needs 60.08/40.10 = 1.498 kg silica and 36.03/40.10 = 0.899 kg carbon per kg SiC. Heat is a floor: the reaction takes 618 kJ per mole SiC (formation enthalpies of SiO2, SiC and CO), 15.4 GJ per tonne, plus about 2.6 GJ to bring the charge to 2300 C, about 18000 MJ, which only resistance heating reaches. Carbon monoxide off-gas heat is not credited, and real furnaces leave unreacted charge, so material yield is optimistic. Crew hours are copied from cement_portland_kg's kiln crew.

alnico_kg.basis: per tonne of cast Alnico permanent-magnet alloy (about 51% Fe, 14% Ni, 8% Al, 24% Co, 3% Cu)
alnico_kg.yield_basis: COMPOSITION. The common Alnico 5 grade is about 24% cobalt, 14% nickel, 8% aluminium, 3% copper and the balance iron, and the inputs are those fractions plus the 2% melt loss bronze_kg uses. Heat is a floor: melting at about 1450 C is 0.5 kJ/kg/K plus 270 kJ/kg fusion, about 990 MJ. Casting, the field anneal and ageing are not modelled. Melt crew hours are copied from bronze_kg. Gated at the cobalt node because the alloy cannot be made before cobalt metal exists.

ferrite_kg.basis: per tonne of sintered manganese ferrite (MnFe2O4) soft magnetic ceramic
ferrite_kg.yield_basis: STOICHIOMETRY. MnFe2O4 is 230.63 g/mol, 69.2% Fe2O3 and 30.8% MnO by mass: 692 kg Fe2O3 and 308 kg MnO. Iron ore is taken at 50% iron as pig_iron_kg does, 71.5% as Fe2O3, giving 968 kg of ore; real ferrite needs purer oxide, so this understates. Pyrolusite is 80% MnO2 as its own entry says, and MnO2 -> MnO + 1/2 O2 needs 1.2255 kg MnO2 per kg MnO, so 377 kg MnO2 and 471 kg ore. Heat is a floor: sintering at about 1250 C is 0.9 kJ/kg/K, about 1100 MJ, plus 1.54 MJ per kg of MnO2 decomposed, about 580 MJ. Labour is copied from ceramic_kg, another pressed and fired ceramic. No single tree node gates this, so requires_node is left absent.

bimetallic_kg.basis: per tonne of roll-bonded thermostat strip, one brass layer and one Invar layer of equal mass
bimetallic_kg.yield_basis: COMPOSITION. A thermostat strip bonds a high-expansion layer (brass) to a low-expansion one (Invar, 64% iron and 36% nickel by mass), here half each by mass: 500 kg brass, 320 kg iron, 180 kg nickel. Trim and scale loss is 8%, the sheet-rolling loss iron_sheet_kg states, giving 540, 346 and 194. Heat is a floor: melting the 500 kg Invar layer at 1450 C is about 490 MJ, and hot-bond rolling at 800 C about 360 MJ, total 850 MJ. Labour is copied from iron_sheet_kg's rolling hours.

mirror_amalgam_kg.basis: per tonne of tin-mercury amalgam laid on plate glass as a mirror backing
mirror_amalgam_kg.yield_basis: COMPOSITION, ASSUMED. The backing is tin foil wetted with mercury; excess mercury is drained and reused, so the layer that stays is a solid amalgam. Its split of 25% tin to 75% mercury by mass is an assumption (no measured source), conf C; the physical statement is that only tin and mercury enter and both are kept in the product. Amalgam is mixed cold, so no heat is listed, and the coating crew is inside the consuming node's own labour.

magnesium_fluoride_kg.basis: per tonne of precipitated magnesium fluoride for optical coatings
magnesium_fluoride_kg.yield_basis: STOICHIOMETRY. MgCl2 + CaF2 + H2SO4 -> MgF2 + CaSO4 + 2 HCl, with fluoride released as hydrogen fluoride from fluorspar and acid. MgF2 is 62.30 g/mol, so per kg: 95.21/62.30 = 1.528 kg MgCl2, 78.07/62.30 = 1.253 kg CaF2 and 98.08/62.30 = 1.574 kg H2SO4, all at an assumed 90% yield: 1698, 1392 and 1749 kg. Hydrochloric acid and calcium sulphate are discarded. Drying and vacuum-grade purification are not modelled. Labour is copied from molybdenum_kg's chemist hours.

mica_kg.basis: per tonne of cleaved sheet mica (muscovite) from a granite pegmatite
mica_kg.yield_basis: EXTRACTED. Useful sheet is a small fraction of the mica-bearing rock; taken as 2% (assumption, so about 50 tonnes of rock per tonne of sheet). Mining hours per tonne of rock are copied from fluorspar_kg (14, hard vein rock), times 50, giving 700. Cleaving and trimming sheets by hand is not costed, a heuristic gap.
